chunks: Wuhayb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who calls to misguidance except that he finds one who follows him.'
ai.seo_question: What happens when someone calls others to misguidance?
ai.summary: In the context of the Gog and Magog (Yajuj and Majuj) narrative, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the spread of misguidance is self-perpetuating, as the inviter inevitably finds adherents who validate and follow their deviation. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of social contagion in spiritual matters, where the 'inviter' (da'i) and the 'follower' (mutabi') form a symbiotic pair in the descent of corruption. The hadith underscores that misguidance is rarely an isolated phenomenon but rather a collective trajectory driven by mutual reinforcement.

en.hubeali: H 14743 – Wuheyb Bin hafs, from Abu Baseer who said:
Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is none from the servants who calls to the misguidance except that he finds the one who follows him’.
en.sarwar: 295. Wuheyb Bin hafs, from Abu Baseer who said:
Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘There is none from the servants who calls to the misguidance except that he finds the one who follows him’.
